questions.q: Find \( \lVert\mathbf{u}\rVert \) for \( \mathbf{u}=(-9,-12) \).
A \( 3 \times 3 \) symmetric matrix \( Q_{k} \) has eigenvalues \( \lambda_1 = 12 \), \( \lambda_2 = 3 \), and \( \lambda_3 = 14 \). Determine the trace \( \text{tr}(Q_{k}) \).
questions.answer: The trace equals \( \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 + \lambda_3 = 29 \).

questions.q: A linear transformation \( T: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2 \) is defined by \( T(\mathbf{x}) = A\mathbf{x} \), where \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). If \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \), find \( T(\mathbf{v}) \).
questions.answer: To find \( T(\mathbf{v}) \), we multiply the matrix \( A \) by the vector \( \mathbf{v} \). \( T(\mathbf{v}) = A\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix} \). Performing the matrix-vector multiplication: \( T(\mathbf{v}) = \begin{pmatrix} (2 \times 1) + (1 \times 2) \\ (1 \times 1) + (3 \times 2) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 + 2 \\ 1 + 6 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} \). Thus, the correct answer is \(\begin{pmatrix} 4 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix}\).

questions.q: Consider the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). If a point \( P=(x,y) \) is transformed by \( A \) to \( P'=(x',y') \), such that \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = A \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \), what is the image of the point \( (3,1) \) under this transformation?
questions.answer:
The transformation is defined by the matrix multiplication \( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = A \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \). We are given the point \( (3,1) \), so \( \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \) and the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \). Performing the matrix multiplication:

\( \begin{pmatrix} x' \\ y' \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} (2 \times 3) + (1 \times 1) \\ (1 \times 3) + (3 \times 1) \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 6 + 1 \\ 3 + 3 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 \\ 6 \end{pmatrix} \)

Therefore, the image of the point \( (3,1) \) is \( (7,6) \).

questions.q: Consider two vectors \( \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix} \). What is the dot product \( \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 \)?
questions.answer:
\( \text{The dot product of two vectors } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} c \\ d \end{pmatrix} \text{ is given by } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = ac + bd. \)

\( \text{In this case, } \mathbf{v}_1 = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \text{ and } \mathbf{v}_2 = \begin{pmatrix} -4 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}. \)

\( \text{Therefore, } \mathbf{v}_1 \cdot \mathbf{v}_2 = (3)(-4) + (4)(3) = -12 + 12 = 0. \)

\( \text{A dot product of 0 indicates that the vectors are orthogonal.} \)

questions.q: Consider the following system of linear equations represented by the augmented matrix: \[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & | & 0 \end{pmatrix} \]. Use row reduction to transform the matrix into row-echelon form and determine the unique solution \( (x, y) \) for the system. What is the value of \( x \)?
questions.answer:
We are given the augmented matrix: \[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & | & 0 \end{pmatrix} \]
To transform this matrix into row-echelon form, we can perform the following row operation: \( R_2 \leftarrow R_2 - 2R_1 \).
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 2 - 2(1) & -1 - 2(2) & | & 0 - 2(5) \end{pmatrix} \]
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & | & -10 \end{pmatrix} \]
Now, we can perform another row operation: \( R_2 \leftarrow R_2 / -5 \).
\[ \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & | & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & | & 2 \end{pmatrix} \]
This matrix is now in row-echelon form. The corresponding system of equations is:
\( x + 2y = 5 \)
\( y = 2 \)
Substitute the value of \( y \) into the first equation:
\( x + 2(2) = 5 \)
\( x + 4 = 5 \)
\( x = 1 \)
Therefore, the unique solution is \( (1, 2) \), and the value of \( x \) is 1.

questions.q: Consider the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} \). Calculate the magnitude of \( \mathbf{v} \), denoted as \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert \).
questions.answer: The magnitude of a vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \) in \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) is given by the formula \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \). For the given vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \\ -12 \end{pmatrix} \), we have \( x=5 \) and \( y=-12 \). Therefore, \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{(5)^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \).

questions.q: Consider the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \). If this vector is plotted on a standard \( xy \)-plane, it represents a directed line segment from the origin to the point \( (3,4) \). What is the geometric interpretation of the length of this vector?
choices: The vector's direction in the xy-plane.
The angle the vector makes with the positive x-axis.
The distance of the point (3,4) from the origin.
The sum of the components of the vector.
questions.answer: The length of a vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix} \) is given by its magnitude, \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \). Geometrically, this corresponds to the distance from the origin \( (0,0) \) to the point \( (x,y) \) on the Cartesian plane, as described by the Pythagorean theorem. For \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix} \), the length is \( \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5 \). This value represents the distance of the point \( (3,4) \) from the origin.

questions.q: Consider the linear transformation \( T: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3 \) defined by \( T(\mathbf{x}) = A\mathbf{x} \), where \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{pmatrix} \). Let \( V \) be the image of \( T \), i.e., \( V = \text{Im}(T) \). \( V \) is a subspace of \( \mathbb{R}^3 \). Find the dimension of the orthogonal complement of \( V \), denoted by \( V^{\perp} \).
questions.answer:
The image of the linear transformation \( T \) is the column space of the matrix \( A \), i.e., \( V = \text{Col}(A) \). The dimension of the image of \( T \) is the rank of the matrix \( A \), i.e., \( \dim(V) = \text{rank}(A) \). We can find the rank of \( A \) by reducing it to row-echelon form:
\[ A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9 \end{pmatrix} \xrightarrow{R_2 \to R_2 - 4R_1, R_3 \to R_3 - 7R_1} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 \\ 0 & -6 & -12 \end{pmatrix} \xrightarrow{R_3 \to R_3 - 2R_2} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -3 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \]
There are two non-zero rows, so the rank of \( A \) is 2. Thus, \( \dim(V) = 2 \). \newline \newline We know that for a subspace \( V \) of \( \mathbb{R}^n \), \( \dim(V) + \dim(V^{\perp}) = n \). In this case, \( n=3 \) and \( \dim(V) = 2 \). Therefore, \( \dim(V^{\perp}) = 3 - \dim(V) = 3 - 2 = 1 \).

questions.q: Consider the vector \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}\) in \(\mathbb{R}^2\). What is the magnitude (or norm) of this vector?
questions.answer: The magnitude (or norm) of a vector \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \\ y \end{pmatrix}\) in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) is given by the formula \(\lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\). For the given vector \(\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \end{pmatrix}\), we have \(x = -3\) and \(y = 4\). Therefore, the magnitude is \(\lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{(-3)^2 + (4)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\).

questions.q: Consider the linear transformation \( T: \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2 \) represented by the matrix \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ k & 4 \end{pmatrix} \). The image of the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \) under this transformation is \( T(\mathbf{v}) = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \). Determine the value of the parameter \( k \).
questions.answer: The linear transformation \( T \) is defined by \( T(\mathbf{x}) = A\mathbf{x} \). We are given \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ k & 4 \end{pmatrix} \) and \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \). The image of \( \mathbf{v} \) is \( T(\mathbf{v}) = A\mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ k & 4 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \cdot 1 + 2 \cdot 1 \\ k \cdot 1 + 4 \cdot 1 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ k+4 \end{pmatrix} \). We are given that \( T(\mathbf{v}) = \begin{pmatrix} 3 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix} \). Equating the components, we have \( 3 = 3 \) (which is consistent) and \( k+4 = 5 \). Solving for \( k \), we get \( k = 5 - 4 = 1 \).

questions.q: Consider a linear transformation \( T: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^2 \) defined by \( T(x,y,z) = (2x - y + z, x + 3y - 2z) \). Let \( V \) be the image of \( T \), i.e., \( V = \text{Im}(T) \). Furthermore, let \( W \) be the subspace of \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) defined by \( W = \{ (a,b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 \mid a+b = 0 \} \). Find the dimension of the intersection of \( V \) and \( W \), i.e., \( \dim(V \cap W) \).
questions.answer:
The linear transformation \( T \) maps \( \mathbb{R}^3 \) to \( \mathbb{R}^2 \). The matrix representation of \( T \) is \( A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \ 1 & 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \). The image of \( T \), denoted as \( V = \text{Im}(T) \), is the column space of \( A \). The columns of \( A \) are \( \begin{pmatrix} 2 \ 1 \end{pmatrix} \), \( \begin{pmatrix} -1 \ 3 \end{pmatrix} \), and \( \begin{pmatrix} 1 \ -2 \end{pmatrix} \). Since these vectors span \( V \), we can find a basis for \( V \) by finding the pivot columns of \( A \) or by noting that the image is a subspace of \( \mathbb{R}^2 \). The rank of \( A \) is 2, which means \( \dim(V) = 2 \). Therefore, \( V = \mathbb{R}^2 \).

The subspace \( W \) is defined by \( W = \{ (a,b) \in \mathbb{R}^2 \mid a+b = 0 \} \). This is the set of vectors in \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) where the sum of the components is zero. A basis for \( W \) can be found by setting \( a = -b \). For example, \( (-1, 1) \) is a basis vector for \( W \). Thus, \( \dim(W) = 1 \).

We are looking for the dimension of \( V \cap W \). Since \( V = \mathbb{R}^2 \), the intersection \( V \cap W \) is simply \( W \). Therefore, \( \dim(V \cap W) = \dim(W) = 1 \).

questions.q: Consider the vector space \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) with the standard dot product. Let \( \mathbf{u} = (3, 4) \) and \( \mathbf{v} = (2, -1) \). Calculate the dot product \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} \).
questions.answer:
The dot product of two vectors \( \mathbf{u} = (u_1, u_2) \) and \( \mathbf{v} = (v_1, v_2) \) in \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) is defined as \( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = u_1v_1 + u_2v_2 \). 
Given \( \mathbf{u} = (3, 4) \) and \( \mathbf{v} = (2, -1) \), we have:
\( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = (3)(2) + (4)(-1) \) 
\( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 6 - 4 \) 
\( \mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v} = 2 \).

questions.q: Consider the vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \ -12 \end{pmatrix} \). Calculate the magnitude of \( \mathbf{v} \), denoted as \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert \).
questions.answer: \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} 5 \ -12 \end{pmatrix} \). The magnitude of a vector \( \mathbf{v} = \begin{pmatrix} x \ y \end{pmatrix} \) in \( \mathbb{R}^2 \) is given by the formula \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} \). Substituting the components of \( \mathbf{v} \): \( \lVert\mathbf{v}\rVert = \sqrt{5^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \).

questions.q: A linear map \( S: \mathbb{R}^{20} \to \mathbb{R}^{28} \) has rank \( \text{rank}(S) = 15 \). Determine the nullity \( \dim(\ker S) \).
questions.answer: By Rank-Nullity, \( \dim(\ker S) = 20 - 15 = 5 \).

questions.q: A planar linear transformation \( S \) scales \( b \) by \( 18 \) and \( y \) by \( 15 \) with matrix \( W = \begin{pmatrix} 18 & 0 \\ 0 & 15 \end{pmatrix} \). Determine the matrix trace \( \text{tr}(W) \).
questions.answer: The trace of the scaling matrix is the sum of its main diagonal entries: \( \text{tr}(W) = 18 + 15 = 33 \).

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}6 & -5\\2 & 3\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (-3A)_{22} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (-3A)_{22}=-3(3)=-9 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -9.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}6 & -4\\4 & -5\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (-2A)_{22} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (-2A)_{22}=-2(-5)=10 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is 10.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}-5 & -1\\-6 & 6\end{matrix}\right] \), \( B=\left[\begin{matrix}-5 & -1\\-1 & -4\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (A+B)_{12} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (A+B)_{12}=(-1)+(-1)=-2 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -2.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}6 & 6\\4 & -3\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (3A)_{21} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (3A)_{21}=3(4)=12 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is 12.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}-3 & -5\\1 & 4\end{matrix}\right] \), \( B=\left[\begin{matrix}-1 & -2\\4 & 6\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (A+B)_{12} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (A+B)_{12}=(-5)+(-2)=-7 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -7.

questions.q: For \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}-1 & 1\\-5 & -2\end{matrix}\right] \), \( B=\left[\begin{matrix}-4 & -5\\-2 & -1\end{matrix}\right] \), find entry \( (A+B)_{22} \).
questions.answer: Applying Matrices & Matrix Algebra principles, \( (A+B)_{22}=(-2)+(-1)=-3 \). Therefore, the verified correct option is -3.
